newsitem.title: UK: UK May retail sales growth lowest since Oct 95-CBI.
newsitem.headline: UK May retail sales growth lowest since Oct 95-CBI.

text.p: The Confederation of British Industry said the annual rate of increase was the lowest reported since October 1995, with 46 percent of retailers reporting higher sales volumes while 25 percent said they were down.
"The three month average indicates underlying sales continue to grow steadily although below the rate of growth reported between June last year and January this," the CBI said.
Retailers reported a slight easing in selling prices with the annual rate of increase at its lowest since August 1995
"The slowdown in sales growth is disappointing for retailers," said Alastair Eperon, chairman of the CBI's distributive trades survey panel.
"However, the survey indicates underlying sales remain on a firmly upward track and retailers are optimistic about business over the short term."
He said the slight easing in price rises expected to be maintain, reflecting "intense price competition among retailers."
